## Introduction
Data growth transformed the way we think about machine learning. What was once small, local experiments done at home on laptops is now big data, scalable pipelines and distributed computing. Cloud platforms like AWS have risen to prominence in today's data science landscape and, AWS is one of them because of its scale and flexibility. In my early years of learning machine learning, I was only interested in learning the models. Performance seems to just make our algorithms better and fine-tune them. But it took me a long while to understand that the real challenge was not just to create the models, it was also to find ways to integrate data management, distribute workloads, scale, deploy the solution and make best use of the new data. That revelation is what brought me into the cloud computing and big data world.

## Cloud Computing and Machine Learning
The cloud technology will deliver something traditional local solutions cannot: elastic resources. Instead of worrying about shortage of hardware, you can build high performance virtual machines, train models on large instances, and shut them down once trained. This pay-as-you-go model is the ideal fit for experimentation and production. AWS makes all parts easy by offering the services that streamline the machine learning pipeline. Everything is integrated, secure and scalable, so you can store raw data in Amazon S3 and train your models with SageMaker. It enables data professionals to work on business solutions instead of infrastructural headaches. Collaboration is also facilitated by cloud computing. Geographically distributed teams can access the same datasets, notebooks and environments. This allows for building large-scale machine learning projects without being tied to any one machine or network.

The Data that underpins machine learning models as they are trained on is just as good data for machine learning modeling. Big data enables models to learn from larger, more complex datasets and produce better predictions. The task, of course, is to process that data swiftly. Combining these tools creates a form which converts data from various sources into a neat, readable form. When ready, it is much easier to train powerful and precise machine learning models.

## Constructing the Machine Learning Models on AWS
SageMaker with AWS is a one-stop solution for the creation and handling of any machine learning model. It gives prebuilt environments for data exploration, training, and deployment. Start out with built-in algorithms or use your own code with tools like TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Scikit-learn. The biggest benefit is scalability. It might take days to train on the local machine, however, SageMaker can also distribute the work on the server across many GPU or CPU instances and complete in a short duration. After training, the model can be deployed as a real-time prediction endpoint. A large part of a Cloud, more than just SageMaker can be serviced by offering AWS services such as Lambda and API Gateway to streamline workflows and serve models to the end user. It builds a seamless pipeline from data ingestion to prediction.

## The Real Value

![](awsservices.png)

Training on AWS on big data and machine learning also taught me a key lesson. The best models are not only accurate, but also realistic. To perform, they must, however, manage real-world data volumes, integrate with other systems, and scale as demand increases. In cloud computing that is feasible. AWS is no longer a nice to know; you need to understand AWS for those who are data scientists or analytics professionals. It’s the bridge between the theory and the art of production. As well as being able to build models, employers appreciate how you also understand infrastructure and deployment of any work you do.

## Final Thoughts
Cloud computing and big data are stretching the frontiers of machine learning, redefining what is possible with it. With AWS, we are provided the tools to easily use big data, training sophisticated models, and deploying them globally, and manage huge data collection. It converts abstract thoughts into working systems with practical consequences for business and research. If you’re interested in learning machine learning, learn how to work in the cloud. Investigate S3 for data storage, EMR for processing, SageMaker for training and usage. This ecosystem works together with a number of tools to bring the user's knowledge from imagination, to actually manufacturing his future designs. AWS is not simply a software platform. It's a connection between data and intelligence, moving us from trial-and-error to result.
